title: Diagnosis and operational resolution
task_statement: Find the cause of a Claude Code problem with built-in diagnostics, usage data, and rewind before you change code or settings. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Diagnostic commands
components.first_principle: Read the loaded state before you change a setting, a hook, or a server, because a file on disk can differ from what loaded.
steps: Run claude doctor in the terminal to find invalid settings files without a session.
Run /doctor inside a session to get proposed fixes that you confirm first.
Run /status to see the settings sources that loaded for the session.
Run /hooks and /mcp to check the hook and server configuration.
Start the session with claude --debug to record each hook match and its exit code.
Run /context to see what fills the context window.
pros: The commands read the live state rather than a remembered setup.
The claude doctor command prints diagnostics and changes nothing.
The debug log shows which hook matchers were checked.
cons: A command shows the state at one moment, so run it again after each change. (Inference)
The diagnostics show what loaded, not why the model chose an action. (Inference)
The debug flag adds log output for the whole session, so use it only for a session that fails. (Inference)
use_when: A setting, hook, or MCP server does not take effect.
Claude Code will not start because a settings file is invalid.
do_not_use_when: The question is about answer quality, and no configuration changed.
A single known setting needs a value change and the file path is clear.

constraints.choice: Run claude doctor before a settings change and again after it.
constraints.combination: Run /doctor in a session when the fix needs Claude to edit files after your confirmation.

constraints.choice: Run /status to confirm that managed settings are in force.
constraints.combination: Check /status on each developer machine after a managed rollout. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Run /context to find large context before you change the model. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Run /compact with focus instructions to free context in the same conversation.

constraints.choice: Enable the debug flag only for the session that fails. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D7.3. Expect a scenario where a hook or a server seems inactive. The credited answer checks the loaded configuration with a built-in command before it edits code or guidance. (Inference)
components.trap: A CLAUDE.md edit meant to make a hook run. Hooks run from settings files, and a guidance note never starts a hook, so the check is the hook configuration and the debug log.
components.decision_rule: Run the built-in check that matches the symptom before you change the setting or the code.
components.exam_tip: If a setting seems ignored, check the settings sources with /status before you edit the file.

components.name: Usage, cost, and telemetry
components.first_principle: Cost and latency changes need per-session numbers before anyone changes the model.
steps: Run /usage in a session to see the session cost and the plan limits.
Set the OpenTelemetry exporter variables in managed settings, the shell, or the user settings file.
Check the claude_code.session.count metric to confirm that the export works.
Track claude_code.cost.usage and claude_code.token.usage in the team backend.
Leave prompt logging off unless the policy allows prompt content in telemetry.
pros: The /usage command shows cost without any setup.
Metrics give a time series for cost and tokens across a team.
Prompt content logging is off by default.
cons: The /usage counters reset when /clear starts a new session.
A repository cannot turn on telemetry, because the repository ignores the OpenTelemetry variables.
Telemetry needs a collector and a backend that the team runs.
use_when: A cost rise needs a trend across sessions and developers.
A developer needs the current session cost in the terminal.
do_not_use_when: The cost question concerns a cloud provider bill, and the provider console is the source of truth.
The team wants prompt text in logs by default, which the default setting blocks.

constraints.choice: Use /usage for the current session and OpenTelemetry for the trend.
constraints.combination: Set workspace spend limits in the Console for an API organization.

constraints.choice: Set the exporter variables in managed settings to lock the collector.
constraints.combination: A repository can only turn a signal off with its exporter selector, not turn telemetry on.

constraints.choice: Keep prompt and response logging off by default.
constraints.combination: Enable prompt logging only where the policy allows prompt content in telemetry.

constraints.choice: Use the default export interval for normal operation.
constraints.combination: Lower the export interval only for a test, and reset it for production. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the cardinality switches to drop session or version attributes from metrics.

components.trap: A smaller model to cut cost before the team reads the usage data. The change may miss the cause and can lower answer quality.
components.decision_rule: Read the cost and token data for the affected sessions before you change the model.

components.name: Rewind and file snapshots
components.first_principle: Rewind restores file edits that Claude Code tracked, so a bad change does not need a manual undo.
steps: Claude Code creates a checkpoint before each prompt that starts a turn.
Claude Code keeps file snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session.
Run /rewind, or press Esc twice with an empty prompt, to open the rewind menu.
Choose the action that restores the conversation, the code, or both.
Use version control for a file that only Bash commands changed, because rewind does not track it.
pros: Rewind undoes tracked Claude edits without a Git command.
The conversation and the code can rewind together.
The rewind menu lists the prompts from the session.
cons: Bash command changes to a file that Claude did not edit are not tracked.
Snapshots are deleted about 30 days after the session last saved one.
A rewind to a deleted snapshot can fail with No files were restored.
use_when: Claude made file edits in the session that you want to undo.
A resumed session needs an earlier file state within the retention period.
do_not_use_when: The change came only from a Bash command on a file that Claude never edited.
The change is older than the retention period for the snapshots.

constraints.choice: Rewind before you send a prompt that repeats the same change. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Set cleanupPeriodDays to keep snapshots longer.

constraints.choice: Keep the repository in version control as the durable record.
constraints.combination: Commit before a large agent change, so Git holds a clean state. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the rewind menu for the most recent checkpoints, which the session keeps.
Review the rewound files before the next commit. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Use version control history as the audit trail for agent edits. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D7.3. Expect a scenario where an agent change must be undone. The credited answer uses rewind for tracked edits and version control for Bash edits. (Inference)
components.trap: A belief that rewind undoes every change in the session. Rewind does not track Bash changes to files that Claude did not edit.
components.decision_rule: Use rewind for tracked Claude edits and version control for everything else.
components.exam_tip: If a stem says a shell command changed a file, look for version control in the answer, not rewind.

key_facts.text: Claude Code keeps file snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Claude Code deletes a session's file snapshots about 30 days after the session last saved one.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Two Esc presses with an empty prompt open the rewind menu.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The cleanupPeriodDays setting sets the retention period, with a default of 30 days.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Rewind does not undo Bash command changes to a file that Claude did not edit.
key_facts.label: Fact
